name: MS Defender Quarantine Manager
description: Ingest Microsoft Defender quarantine emails through Azure Automation into native SOAR or ES workflows. Inspect, release or deny quarantine messages.

actions.description: Read-only inspection of the deployed runbook, loaded Exchange cmdlet contract, and one exact quarantine identity; optional tenant RBAC inspection requires explicit opt-in
actions.verbose: Fires the Azure Automation webhook with action=diagnose. The runbook binds the exact Get-QuarantineMessage identity before any optional tenant-wide RBAC query. By default it reads only the identity and local runtime/cmdlet metadata. When include_rbac=true, it additionally reads management-role contracts, the Quarantine role and assignments, managed-identity app/object GUIDs, the matching Exchange service principal, and relevant role-group membership. Only GUID-confirmed matching group names cross into the result; unrelated assignment names and members remain private. Permission-query totals count every real failure while retained records are capped at 20 and 32 KiB of compact UTF-8 JSON. It never returns an access token or xms_mirid resource path and never invokes Release-QuarantineMessage. Also collects bounded, redacted static source from the loaded Release-QuarantineMessage proxy and same-module forwarding helpers, plus ActionType type/enum/ValidateSet metadata. Source availability and truncation are explicit. No HTTP request capture or command invocation occurs.

identity.description: Exact quarantine Identity in GUID1\GUID2 form. The diagnose action reads this identity but never releases or denies it.

include_rbac.description: Explicitly opt in to tenant-wide read-only RBAC and role-group diagnostics after the exact quarantine identity has been bound. Defaults to false.

actions.description: Release a quarantined message to all original recipients
actions.verbose: Runs one Azure Automation job for release. The runbook checks the exact identity is Requested, then executes Release-QuarantineMessage -Identity <id> -ReleaseToAll -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction Stop once. After a successful command it waits for Released using bounded status reads (default seven checks, ten seconds apart). The app waits for the same Azure job within the configured budget (default 600 seconds, status polling every five seconds). Errors include the known job ID and original cause. A timeout does not cancel the Azure job or prove that Exchange performed no action. No automatic writing retry, later recovery or operation ID is required. A deliberately started new action is a new request. Use inspect release environment only when manual diagnosis is wanted. A same-identity conflict on the shared SOAR execution host submits no job. Consult summary.outcome and data.error_code; never retry pending or unknown results before inspection.

identity.description: Quarantine message Identity in the exact format GUID1\GUID2 (e.g. c14401cf-aa9a-465b-cfd5-08d0f0ca37c5\4c2ca98e-94ea-db3a-7eb8-3b63657d4db7). Use container:data.quarantine_identity from the ingested SOAR event (the linked SOAR container for an ES finding). The format is validated before the webhook fires - malformed values fail immediately without starting a runbook job.
